title: Event 1: The 2026 Field Just Cut the First-Ever Games Workout in Half
dek: The Games opened with the EXACT workout from 2007. Jay Crouch (7:11) and Maddy Sturt (8:03) didn't just win Event 1 - they nearly halved the marks the sport set 19 years ago. Sturt's time would have beaten the 2007 men's champion by five minutes.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: Event 1 of the 2026 Games, "the 2007 Hopper," is the exact workout (same reps, same loads) that opened the inaugural 2007 Games - a rare apples-to-apples measure of how far the sport has come. Jay Crouch won it in 7:11 (vs Brett Marshall's 13:07 in 2007) and Madeline Sturt in 8:03 (vs Jolie Gentry's 16:22). Both winners are Australian. The best woman today is now over five minutes faster than the best man was when the sport began.

blocks.text: The 20th CrossFit Games opened by reaching all the way back to the first one. **Event 1, 'the 2007 Hopper,' is the exact workout that opened the inaugural 2007 Games** - same reps, same loads, right down to the 135/85 lb push jerks. That makes today a rare, clean measurement: the identical test, run by the best in the world, 19 years apart. The result is staggering.
The Same Test, Two Different Sports

The workout, both times: **1,000-meter row, then 5 rounds of 25 pull-ups and 7 push jerks** (135 lb men / 85 lb women), for time. In 2007 it was **drawn at random from a literal hopper** - a peanut roaster filled with colored balls - on the morning of competition, in front of an **open-registration field** (anyone could sign up; about 44 men and 20 women showed) on the **Castro family ranch**, with **$500** to the winner. Tonight it was Event 1 of a sold-out professional championship, known and trained for in advance. Same barbell. A completely different world.
Then vs Now: The Numbers Are Brutal

In 2007, the fastest man on this workout was **Brett Marshall in 13:07**. Tonight, **Jay Crouch won it in 7:11** - **nearly six minutes faster**, 45% quicker than anything the sport could produce in 2007. The women's gap is even bigger: **Jolie Gentry's winning 16:22** became **Madeline Sturt's 8:03** - she **more than halved it**, 8 minutes and 19 seconds faster. And the stat that says everything about two decades of progress: **Sturt's 8:03 would have beaten the 2007 men's champion by over five minutes.** The best woman in the field today is comfortably faster than the best man was when the sport began.

blocks.text: Why the Gap Is This Enormous

It is not that today's athletes are simply 45% 'fitter.' It is that the sport professionalized. In 2007, CrossFit was a garage-gym experiment - the competitors held day jobs, trained without specialized programming, and had never seen the workout until it came out of the hopper. In 2026, these are **full-time professional athletes** with dedicated coaches, sport science, nutrition and recovery, and years of training built for exactly this test. The workout did not change. The human being doing it did. That is the whole story of the Sport of Fitness in one head-to-head.
An Engaged Couple, Two Wins

Here is the detail that turns a great opener into a story: **Jay Crouch and Madeline Sturt are engaged** - and they BOTH won Event 1, the men's and the women's, to open the Games. Two Australians, one household, two event wins on day one. You could not script a better start. The full Event 1 top 10 and the overall leaderboard are on the site.

title: Day 1 Is Here: 7 Events, One Brutal Wednesday
dek: The 2026 Games open with a seven-event gauntlet across the Bay Area - an engine-and-strength sandwich with no place for specialists to hide. And Ricky Garard may have drawn the dream card.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: Day 1 of the 2026 CrossFit Games (Wednesday, July 22) is SEVEN scored individual events, run off-site across the Bay Area at The Ranch in Aromas and the Morgan Hill Outdoor Complex. Six are revealed - the 2007 Hopper, Ranch 7200, the three-part CrossFit Total, and the Grass Oval Bicycle Race - and a seventh is a FloElite exclusive still under wraps. Here is the running order, the storylines, and why Ricky Garard could bank an early lead.

blocks.text: It starts tomorrow. Day 1 of the 2026 Games, **Wednesday July 22**, is not an easing-in: it is **seven scored individual events** run across the Bay Area at **The Ranch (Aromas)** and the **Morgan Hill Outdoor Complex**, women's heats first and men's right behind, from morning into the night. Six events are already public; the seventh is a **FloElite exclusive** whose workout is still under wraps. That is a brutal opening day - and it is built so that neither the pure engine nor the pure strength athlete can hide.
The Running Order

blocks.text: Garard's Dream Draw

If you are building a Day 1 for **Ricky Garard**, it looks like this. He **won the 7,200 m trail run at the 2025 Games** - literally Event 2 again - and he is our **favorite for the bike race** (a former BMX racer who won the 2022 Bike to Work). Two of tomorrow's seven events are tests he has already conquered. Add a respectable Total and a strong Hopper and the man who finished **2nd overall in 2025** could walk out of Wednesday with a real lead before the arena doors even open. The rest of the podium contenders have to keep him in sight.
The Total Is Where Medals Move

Three of the seven events are the **CrossFit Total**, and because each 1-rep-max is scored as its own 50-point event, the strength block is where the standings swing hardest. This is the day the true heavyweights - the athletes with verified squat, press and deadlift numbers - bank points that the engine specialists simply cannot match on a barbell. Our CrossFit Total boards break down exactly who is armed for it. Everyone else has to survive the strength day without bleeding too much ground.
An Engine-and-Strength Sandwich

Look at the shape of the day: an engine-and-gymnastics opener (Hopper), a long run (Ranch 7200), a maximal-strength block (the Total), a bike race (Event 6), and a mystery closer (Event 7). Pure strength athletes get exposed on the run and the bike; pure engines give ground on the Total. The athletes who climb the Day 1 leaderboard will be the true generalists - which is, of course, the whole point of the Sport of Fitness. Full model reads for every revealed event are linked on the site.

title: Roll to Support AMRAP: The Ring Test Castro Teased Is Now Fully Scored
dek: The two ring skills the Games have never tested now have a full prescription on the official workouts page: a 5-minute AMRAP of forward and backward rolls to support, on the final day. We already researched who has the gymnastics background - here is the scored event.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: The official CrossFit Games workouts page has published the full scored prescription for the ring skills Dave Castro teased in July: a 5-minute AMRAP of 4 forward rolls to support and 3 backward rolls to support, presented by Velites, scheduled for Sunday, July 26, the Games' final day. Both movements have zero precedent in Games history (2007-2025). We already researched every athlete's real gymnastics background for the earlier tease; here is that read applied to the confirmed AMRAP.

blocks.text: The official CrossFit Games workouts page has published the full scored version of the ring test Dave Castro teased in July. It is a **5-minute AMRAP**: **4 forward rolls to support**, **3 backward rolls to support**, repeated for max rounds and reps. Presented by **Velites, the Official Grip of the CrossFit Games**, and scheduled for **Sunday, July 26**, the competition's final day. This is the scored prescription for the two ring skills Castro revealed on the **Girls Unfiltered podcast** in July (demoed by Trista Smith and Jacob Marlow) as movements the Games have **never tested before**: a forward roll to support and a backward roll to support on the still rings.
Zero Precedent, By Design

A case-insensitive search of every Games event from 2007 through 2025 in our own results archive turns up **zero prior instances** of a roll-to-support movement, forward or backward. This is a genuinely new test. But the underlying skill base is not foreign to this field: every 2026 qualifier already owns strict ring muscle-ups, skin-the-cats and strict ring handstand push-ups, the base CrossFit itself lists as prerequisites for the backward roll to support. An AMRAP format also changes the read from the original tease: instead of a single high-control pass, this rewards whoever can hold clean rotation and a locked-out support for five minutes straight, deep into Sunday fatigue.
The Men: Three Real Gymnasts at the Top

When we researched actual gymnastics backgrounds for the original tease, the list reshuffled away from the season model. **Patrick Vellner** competed on apparatus into 2010 and remains the field's cleanest technician. **Victor Hoffer** trained federation-level artistic gymnastics in France from age 3, roughly 20 hours a week - his 44 gymnastics score this season badly undersells him, and a pure ring-rotation AMRAP is built for him. **Roman Khrennikov** came through a Russian Olympic-reserve gymnastics program plus break-dancing floorwork. Behind them, **Justin Medeiros** brings the field's sharpest strict-ring control, and **Colten Mertens** plays in the United Grid League, where the backward roll to support is a standard skill - one of the two movements may not be new to him at all.

title: Machine 7200M: Row 3,600, Ski 3,600 - Whose Engine Survives the Double?
dek: The official workouts page has published a pure double-machine test with no exact match in Games history. We found the two closest precedents in our own archive - and one athlete who has already won both.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: The official CrossFit Games workouts page has published Machine 7200M: for time, row 3,600 meters then ski 3,600 meters, under a 30-minute cap for men and 35 minutes for women, presented by Saatva and scheduled for Sunday, July 26. No prior Games event pairs a full row and a full ski leg, but the two closest precedents in our archive - the 2020 Stage 1 1,000m Row and the 2022 Rinse 'N' Repeat swim/SkiErg interval - name a men's double machine-event winner already in the 2026 field.

blocks.text: The official CrossFit Games workouts page has published **Machine 7200M**. The prescription, quoted exactly: **"For time: Row 3,600 meters, Ski 3,600 meters."** Time cap is **30 minutes for men, 35 minutes for women**. Presented by **Saatva, the Official Sleep Partner of the CrossFit Games**, and scheduled for **Sunday, July 26**, the Games' final day. Two full 3,600-meter legs back to back, on two different machines, is 7,200 total meters of pure monostructural output with nothing else in the workout: no barbell, no gymnastics, just pacing across two disciplines.
A Double Machine Test With No Exact Precedent

A search of every Games event from 2007 to 2025 in our own archive turns up **no prior event that pairs a full row leg and a full ski leg** the way Machine 7200M does. The closest match is the 2016 Rope Chipper, a five-station event that included short row and ski segments alongside a bike, double-unders and a sled pull - not a clean two-machine test. The real precedent has to be assembled from the pieces: the Games have tested a **pure row sprint** once (2020) and a **swim-plus-SkiErg interval** once (2022). Neither is Machine 7200M, but both tell us who has already been fast on these exact machines under Games pressure.
The Two Closest Tests on Record

**2020 Stage 1: 1,000-Meter Row.** A single maximal row, contested remotely during the pandemic-era online stage. **Roman Khrennikov** won the men's event outright in **2:48.90**, competing from Russia. **Karin Freyová** won the women's in **3:15.80** over Amanda Barnhart, but Freyová is not part of the 2026 field. **2022 Games: Rinse 'N' Repeat.** An 8-round interval pairing a 50-yard swim with rising SkiErg calorie targets, then a max-effort finish - the closest thing to a row/ski-style double-machine grind the Games have actually run. Khrennikov won that event too, with **160 calories**, his first-ever Games win. **Lucy Campbell** won the women's side with **137 calories**, her first Games event win.
The Men: Khrennikov Owns Both Machines

**Roman Khrennikov** is the only athlete in the 2026 field who has won a Games machine event outright, and he has done it twice: the 2020 row sprint and the 2022 swim/SkiErg interval. **Patrick Vellner** was 7th in the 2020 row (2:54.80), the fastest 2026 qualifier in that field after Khrennikov. **Justin Medeiros** was 7th in the 2022 interval (151 cal) and 15th in the 2020 row (2:59.00) - real mileage on both machines. **Jeffrey Adler** placed 11th in the 2020 row (2:57.30) and 13th in 2022 (146 cal), consistent across both tests. **Ricky Garard** was 10th in the 2022 interval (147 cal) and is the reigning runner-up overall.

title: Event 6: The Grass Oval Bicycle Race Is Set. Whose Legs Are Built for It?
dek: CrossFit's official workouts page has revealed the full Day 1 cycling test: 20 laps of a grass oval, 25 minutes, at Morgan Hill. Here's who has already won this exact format, and who the season model likes now.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: Individual Event 6 of the 2026 Games is the Grass Oval Bicycle Race: 20 laps for time under a 25-minute cap, Wednesday July 22 at the Morgan Hill Outdoor Complex. We checked the field's real history in the Games' three prior dedicated bike races (2017 Cyclocross, 2018 Crit, 2023 Ride) plus the bike-and-gymnastics 2022 Bike to Work, and modeled the rest, with a data-grounded top 5 for men and women.

blocks.text: The official CrossFit Games workouts page has published the field's Day 1 cycling test: the **Grass Oval Bicycle Race**. Twenty laps of a grass oval track, for time, under a **25-minute cap**, at the **Morgan Hill Outdoor Complex** on Wednesday, July 22. Zenni Optical presents. This is the full reveal of the 'Ride' cycling opener CrossFit teased in June, and the official CrossFit Games Instagram has since confirmed it as **Individual Event 6**. Unlike a stationary Echo-bike sprint, a bike race on grass rewards something almost nobody in this field has trained: real bike handling.
A Grind on Two Wheels, Not a Sprint

Twenty laps for time, with no per-lap distance announced, sits closer to the Games' two dedicated road-bike races than to a short sprint. The 2017 Cyclocross (three laps, roughly 19 to 21 minutes for the leaders) and the 2018 Crit (ten laps of a ~1,200m loop, roughly 18 to 20 minutes) both ran in that window under similar caps. Expect the Grass Oval Bicycle Race to land in the same range: a sustained aerobic effort of somewhere between 15 and 25 minutes, decided by leg power, bike-handling through repeated turns on an oval, and pacing, not a single burst. No barbell, no gymnastics skill involved: this is pure engine.
The Games Have Asked This Question Before

Cycling has real history at the Games, and unlike most 2026 tests, several current qualifiers have already answered a version of this exact question. **Jeffrey Adler** finished 2nd in the 2023 Ride (mountain-bike laps at Rogue's Alliant Energy Center) and 4th in the 2022 Bike to Work; no one else in the 2026 field has two finishes that strong across dedicated bike tests. **Ricky Garard** won the 2022 Bike to Work outright. On the women's side, **Emma Lawson** owns the strongest bike resume of anyone in the 2026 field, either division: she won the 2023 Ride and finished 3rd in the 2022 Bike to Work. **Haley Adams** won that same 2022 race. **Patrick Vellner** has started every one of the Games' four dedicated bike tests since 2017 (13th, 35th, 20th, 27th) without ever cracking the front of that specific board: real mileage, not real precedent. Note that 2022's Bike to Work paired the bike with pull-ups, so it is a partial comp; the 2017 Cyclocross, 2018 Crit and 2023 Ride are the closest matches to a pure bike race.
The Men: Adler's Resume, Garard's Win

**Jeffrey Adler** tops this board on history alone: a runner-up finish in the 2023 Ride plus 4th in 2022, the most consistent bike-specific record in the field. **Ricky Garard** WON the 2022 race outright and also carries the best modeled engine-and-sprint blend of anyone with proven bike results. **Justin Medeiros** was 3rd in 2022 and owns the single highest engine-and-sprint blend in the entire men's field, history or no history. **James Sprague** has no verified bike-race placement in our data (he finished 2023 outside the top 10 overall, so his per-event result isn't in the official leaderboard cohort we track), but his modeled engine and sprint numbers are third-best among the men. **Patrick Vellner** closes the five on sheer repetition: four separate bike starts since 2017, an elite modeled sprint score, and still no finish better than 13th on this specific test.

title: Rookie Watch: Bergros Bjornsdottir, the Gymnast Who Medals as a Weightlifter
dek: Our model calls the 19-year-old Icelandic rookie a gymnast and rates her heavy work dead last. Her weightlifting medals call her something else entirely. Both are true - here is what that means in San Jose.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: Bergros Bjornsdottir, 19, is Iceland's only individual qualifier and a Games rookie who got the call two weeks after the submission window closed, moving into the field as a replacement after the post-lock penalties. Our model ranks her 17th of 30 women, driven by 100th-percentile bodyweight gymnastics and dragged down by 17th-percentile heavy and sprint work. But she is also Iceland's first-ever medallist at a global weightlifting championship, with a competition-verified 88 kg (194 lb) snatch and 110 kg (242 lb) clean and jerk. We reconcile the two readings.

blocks.text: Every Games has a rookie nobody outside the sport is watching yet. This year one of them is **Bergros Bjornsdottir**, 19, from Selfoss, Iceland, competing out of **CrossFit Reykjavik** and the **only Icelandic athlete in the individual field**. Her path here is the storyline: she finished **7th at the Individual Online Semifinal**, just outside an automatic berth, then got an email from CrossFit **two weeks after the submission window had already closed** telling her she was in, moving up as a replacement after the post-lock penalties reshaped the women's field. A rookie who backed into the Games on paper, and who is far more dangerous than that sentence sounds.
The Model Says Gymnast

Our projection ranks her **17th of 30** women at a 66.2 capacity score, and the shape of that number is lopsided. Her **bodyweight gymnastics sit at the 100th percentile of this field** - the single best mark on her card - built on a **1st place on Quarterfinal Test 1** and a **3rd on Open 26.1**. When the test is high-skill and self-powered, she is elite already. Her softest area is the mirror image: **heavy and sprint-length work at the 17th percentile**, the lowest score on her profile. On the model alone, she reads as a pure gymnast with an honest strength gap.
Her Medals Say Weightlifter

Except the model has never seen her on a platform. Before CrossFit took over, Bjornsdottir was a weightlifter - and not a casual one. She is **Iceland's first-ever medallist at a global weightlifting championship**, the **2024 IWF Youth World Championships in Lima** (women's 71 kg), where she finished a hair short of the overall title in a story the IWF headlined "six days ago she couldn't walk." Her competition bests, verified in the official meet database, are an **88 kg snatch (194 lb)** and a **110 kg clean and jerk (242 lb)**. For context that matters this weekend: her 194 lb snatch would **clear the 185 lb top bar of the Speed Snatch Triple** (Event 15). This is not a gymnast who happens to lift. This is a decorated lifter who happens to do gymnastics.
So Which Reading Is Right? Both.

The two are not in conflict once you separate **absolute load** from **barbell skill**. The model's 17th-percentile "heavy" score measures raw output on the field's heaviest sleds, sandbags and long grinders, where 75 kg athletes simply move more total mass than a lightweight - and it is right that she gives ground there. What the model cannot price is that her barbell technique under fatigue is genuinely elite for her size. Give her a **max-effort or ascending-snatch test**, a high-skill gymnastics chipper, or anything that rewards a clean fast bar over brute tonnage, and the rookie you filed under "17th" is a threat to win the event. Give her a heavy sandbag sprint and she is chasing. That split - dangerous on skill and speed, exposed on absolute strength - is exactly the profile of a 19-year-old who has not filled out yet, and it is why she is worth watching now rather than in 2028.

title: Castro's Ring Test: Two New Skills, and the Gymnasts Built for Them
dek: Rings take center stage midday Sunday with two skills the Games have never tested. The whole field owns the base and has two weeks to drill them, so this is not a wildcard: it rewards the real gymnasts. We checked every athlete's background.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: Dave Castro revealed two never-before-tested ring gymnastics skills for a midday Sunday event: a ring muscle-up into a forward roll to support, and a backward roll to support. The whole field already owns the base movements and has two weeks to drill the new ones, so it is not a wildcard. We researched every athlete's real gymnastics background to see who is positioned.

blocks.text: Dave Castro just handed the 2026 Games a curveball. On the **Girls Unfiltered** podcast and in a social post demoed by Trista Smith and Jacob Marlow, he unveiled **two ring gymnastics skills the Games have never tested**: a **ring muscle-up straight into a forward roll**, finishing locked out in a support at the top, and a **backward roll to support** with the arms locked out on the rings. Both land **midday Sunday**, the final day, when athletes are deepest into fatigue. His message was blunt: control and strength on the rings will help decide the Fittest on Earth.
What the Two Skills Actually Are

The first chains a **ring muscle-up**, already a Games staple, directly into a **forward roll** on the rings, ending locked out in support at the top: one continuous, high-control sequence rather than a stop-and-reset. The second, the **backward roll to support**, is a still-rings skill where the athlete rolls backward through the rings to finish in a straight-arm support. It is rare in CrossFit but a **staple of the United Grid League**, where teams drill it. CrossFit's own coaching notes list real prerequisites for it: confident ring dips, a strict muscle-up, and genuine body control. These are not volume movements. They are precision under fatigue.
Why This Rewards the Gymnasts, Not a Wildcard

Here is the part that got called a wildcard, and why that misses. **Every athlete in this field already owns the base these skills are built on**: strict ring muscle-ups, skin-the-cats, and strict ring handstand push-ups. The two new pieces are **additions on top of that base, not a foreign language**. And nobody walks in cold: the field has roughly **two weeks to drill them**. So this is not a skill nobody can do. It is a skill everyone can build, which turns it into a test of **who builds it fastest and cleanest**, and that rewards a real gymnastics background and the sharpest ring control. Two weeks is enough time to make it a show, not a wipeout.
We Checked the Backgrounds

Our model scores gymnastics off this season's results, and a season score can miss a real gymnast having an off year. So we went past the model and **researched every athlete's actual background**: who was a competitive artistic gymnast, a tumbler or trampolinist, a diver, a parkour athlete, or a known rings specialist. The list reshuffled. On the men's side the top of the read is **three genuine former gymnasts**. **Patrick Vellner** competed on apparatus into 2010 and is the field's cleanest technician. **Victor Hoffer** trained federation-level artistic gymnastics in France from age 3, roughly 20 hours a week; his 44 gymnastics score this season badly undersells him and this event is built for him. **Roman Khrennikov** came through a Russian Olympic-reserve gymnastics program plus break-dancing floorwork. Behind them sit the sharpest technicians: **Justin Medeiros**, whose wrestling gives a direct rolling instinct, and **Colten Mertens**, who plays in the United Grid League where the backward roll to support is a standard skill, so one of the two new movements may not be new to him at all.

The women's read moved even more. The model's proxy favored big bodyweight-strength numbers, but **strength is not the same as rotation**. The athletes built for this are the real gymnasts and ring specialists: **Madeline Sturt**, Australia's premier rings athlete, whose 47 gymnastics score completely hides her ring control; **Abigail Domit**, a USAG Level 9 artistic gymnast; **Ella Wilkinson**, who tumbled and trampolined for Team GB to age 15; **Danielle Brandon**, a childhood gymnast and state diver; and **Haley Adams** and **Alexis Raptis**, both former competitive artistic gymnasts. A powerful athlete without that background can still grind these out, but the rolls look sharpest on the athletes who have been rolling and inverting since childhood.

title: Day 1 of the 2026 Games Is Five Events. Who Survives Them All?
dek: The Games open at the Ranch with a metcon, a 7.2km run and three max lifts, all in one day. We modeled who has the breadth to survive it, and who gets exposed.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: The 2026 CrossFit Games open with five scored events on Day 1 (Wednesday July 22): The 2007 Hopper, Ranch 7200 and The CrossFit Total. We built a Day-1 breadth score from the model to find who covers a metcon, a 7.2km run and three max lifts best, and who gets exposed by the day's contradictions.

blocks.text: The 2026 Games do not ease anyone in. On **Day 1, Wednesday July 22**, at the off-site venues around the Ranch in Aromas, the individual field faces **five scored events**: **The 2007 Hopper** (Event 1, a row-and-rig metcon), **Ranch 7200** (Event 2, a 7,200-meter trail run), and **The CrossFit Total** (Events 3-5, max back squat, shoulder press and deadlift). A metcon, an endurance run, and a strength triple, all before anyone touches the SAP Center floor. It is the broadest opening day the Games have programmed, and the demands actively fight each other.
The Contradiction Built Into Day 1

Look at what these five events ask for. The Hopper wants a gymnastics engine and grip. Ranch 7200 wants a deep aerobic motor and a **light frame** to carry over 4.5 miles. The Total wants the opposite: raw, **absolute strength**, where more body mass is an asset. A 65 kg runner and a 100 kg squatter are almost different species, and Day 1 asks every athlete to be both. Nobody wins all five. The athlete who wins the day is the one with no hole for it to find, so we scored the field on breadth: how well each covers all six domains these events tax, weighted 70 percent on the average and 30 percent on their single weakest domain, because one crack is fatal when the day tests everything.
The Men: Medeiros Is Built for This

Run the five events through the model and one name sits on top: **Justin Medeiros**. The two-time champion reads top-three in the metcon, the run, and the strength triple, and he has **no soft domain, nothing below the 77th percentile** across gymnastics, engine, monostructural, aerobic, heavy strength and Olympic lifting. That is the definition of a Day-1 athlete. **Roman Khrennikov** is right behind on a monster engine and elite lifting; his only relative give is the long run, the one event where his size is a tax. **Ricky Garard** has no weak domain either, while **Patrick Vellner** pairs huge gymnastics and strength with the one crack the run can widen, his engine.

The women's read splits into engines and all-arounders. **Emma Lawson** tops the breadth score because she has no weakness, nothing under the 67th percentile across all five events. **Haley Adams** and **Lucy Campbell** own the two biggest engines in the field and should lead the Hopper and the run, but they share the same hole: the back squat and deadlift. The Total is where the strength day claws back what they bank early. **Mirjam von Rohr** is the interesting one, pairing the field's best raw engine with a record-setting back squat, the rare woman who can score on the run AND the strength, which is why the model likes her Day-1 shape.

The venue is the story too. Day 1 runs at the Aromas ranch, the birthplace of the Games from 2007 to 2009, and the programming leans all the way into it: the 2007 Hopper revives the very first Games event, and the original hopper apparatus is back. Opening the sport's 20th-anniversary Games where it started, with a run on the same dirt, is a deliberate homecoming before the lights of San Jose take over July 24-26.

title: The CrossFit Total: Who Tops Each Lift, and the Whole Thing
dek: Events 3, 4 and 5 are three 50-point lifts. We pulled the athletes real competition maxes and built a leaderboard for each, plus the overall Total.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: Events 3-5 of the 2026 CrossFit Games are The CrossFit Total: 1RM back squat, shoulder press and deadlift, each a 50-point event. We built a leaderboard for every lift from real competition maxes (the 2025 Games back squat, the 2023 Rogue deadlift, the 2020 Games press) plus reported PRs and labeled estimates, then summed them for the overall Total.

blocks.text: Events 3, 4 and 5 are **The CrossFit Total**, three separate 50-point events: a 1-rep-max back squat, strict shoulder press and deadlift. So instead of guessing, we went to the tape. We pulled these athletes actual competition maxes, the **2025 CrossFit Games 1-rep-max back squat**, the **2023 Rogue Invitational** and **2026 World Fitness Project** max deadlifts, and the strict presses from the **2020 Games Total**, then filled the gaps with official reported PRs and clearly labeled self-reported stats. **Colten Mertens** owns this one on real evidence: he **won the 2025 Games 1-rep-max back squat at 570 lb**, breaking an 18-year Games record. **Nick Mathew** (555) and **Justin Medeiros** (512) also squatted big in that same 2025 test; **Austin Hatfield** (535) and **Guilherme Malheiros** (511) sit on reported PRs. The women are led by another 2025 Games result: **Mirjam von Rohr won that event at 360 lb**, with **Anikha Greer** tied second at 355, then **Elisa Fuliano** (353) and **Kyra Milligan** (340) on profile numbers.

summary: Event 1 of the 2026 CrossFit Games is The 2007 Hopper: a 1,000m row then 5 rounds of 25 pull-ups and 7 push jerks. We modeled whose profile the workout rewards, with a data-grounded top 5 for men and women.

blocks.text: Event 1 pulls a fossil out of the vault. It is **The 2007 Hopper**, the workout that opened the very first CrossFit Games: a 1,000-meter row, then 5 rounds of 25 pull-ups and 7 push jerks, for time. The barbell sits at 135 lb for the men and 85 lb for the women. Everything else is you against gravity. The row and the pull-ups carry no load at all. Individuals kick it off Wednesday, July 22, 2026. Read the pieces and the shape is clear: this is a medium-length grind, not a sprint and not a marathon. The 2007 winner needed about 13 minutes; when the field ran it back in 2013 the top time dropped to 8:33. The engine gets lit early on the rower, then the day becomes a math problem, 125 total pull-ups against 35 light push jerks. The barbell is almost a formality. Whoever can cycle pull-ups in big unbroken chunks while breathing hard controls this.
The Men: Two Co-Favorites, One Light Barbell

The model likes **Roman Khrennikov** and **Justin Medeiros** at the top, and they sit within about two points of each other. Treat them as co-favorites, because the order hinges on how much you weight that light barbell. Khrennikov leads on the strength of a **90 Bodyweight** score paired with an **81 Metabolic** and a **79 Long Engine**, the exact three things this workout hammers. Medeiros trails by a hair with the more even card: **80 Weightlifting**, **77 Gymnastics**, **78 Metabolic**. If the 135 lb push jerk matters more than the fatigue math suggests, Medeiros closes the gap and passes him. Behind the two, Ricky Garard, Patrick Vellner, and James Sprague are bunched. Garard's profile is balanced with no soft spot on the bodyweight side (77). Vellner owns the best gymnastics number in this group at 78 but the lowest long engine at 66, so a longer grind works against him. Sprague, the youngest read here, is carried by a 79 Bodyweight and steady metabolic work.

title: Event 2 Is a 7,200m Ranch Run. Whose Engine Fits It?
dek: The second event sends the field off-road for a 7.2km trail run. We modeled whose aerobic engine, and whose body mass, the Ranch rewards.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: Event 2 of the 2026 CrossFit Games is Ranch 7200: a 7,200-meter trail run at the Aromas ranch where the Games were born. We modeled whose profile a long run rewards, scaling the aerobic read by power-to-weight, with a data-grounded top 5 for men and women.

blocks.text: Event 2 takes the 2026 CrossFit Games off-road. On the opening day at the Aromas ranch, the patch of California where the Games were born in 2007, the field faces **Ranch 7200**: a 7,200-meter trail run, for time. That is about 4.5 miles of dirt and hills. It is the purest endurance test the Games have run in years, and it rewards two things a barbell never asks for: a deep aerobic engine and a light frame to carry it. Individuals run it Wednesday, July 22, right after the opener.
A Run Rewrites the Board

Here is the honest problem with modeling a run: nothing in the 2026 season was a run. The Open and Quarterfinals were indoor, machine-and-barbell affairs, so we do not have a measured 7km time for anyone. What we do have is each athlete's long engine (sustained output), their monostructural machine output, and their oxidative-system score, all computed from real results. That is the right starting point. Then we adjust for the one thing a trail run punishes that a rower does not: body mass. Over 7.2km, every extra kilogram is a kilogram carried the whole way. So the read below is an aerobic-engine ranking scaled by power-to-weight, not a stopwatch.
The Men: Adler's Frame Beats Khrennikov's Engine

The biggest engine in the men's field belongs to **Roman Khrennikov**, an 81 monostructural with elite sustained output. On a rower or a bike, he wins this. But at a corrected **103 kilograms**, a 7.2km run is where his size is a bill that comes due, and the mass-adjusted read drops him to the back of the top five. The pick at the top is **Justin Medeiros**: a 79 oxidative engine on an **88-kilogram** frame, the best blend of motor and manageable mass in the field. **Ricky Garard** (corrected 93 kg) and **James Sprague** (95 kg) follow on strong engines. **Jeffrey Adler** slots **fourth, not first**: his weight was mis-listed at 72 kg but the official record is **197 lb (89 kg)**, essentially Medeiros's mass without the same aerobic ceiling, so the run is a hold-serve event for him rather than the runaway an earlier read implied.

blocks.text: The Women: Adams Runs Away From the Field

On the women's side it is not close. **Haley Adams** owns the single biggest engine in either division, an 82 long engine, and carries it at 64 kilograms. Best motor, lightest relevant frame: on a run, that is the dream combination, and she is the clear model pick. **Emma Lawson**, also 64 kilograms with a balanced aerobic card, is second. **Mirjam von Rohr** posts the field's highest raw engine score at 83 and lands third; a long run is the kind of event where her sustained output can shine even against lighter athletes. **Lucy Campbell** (81 engine) and **Danielle Brandon** (75 monostructural, and a better runner than her reputation) complete the five.

blocks.text: Meanwhile, Back at the Ranch

Opening here is not a gimmick, it is a homecoming. The Ranch in Aromas hosted the first three CrossFit Games from 2007 to 2009, on Dave Castro's family property, until the sport outgrew the field. Trail running is woven through Games history too: a roughly seven-kilometer trail run opened Games competition in 2016. Ranch 7200 stitches both threads together, the birthplace and the run, onto the opening day of the sport's 20th-anniversary Games, right alongside the revived 2007 Hopper that runs as Event 1.

blocks.text: There was no run in the 2026 season, so no athlete has a measured 7km time. This read starts from competition-derived performance profiles, long engine (sustained output), monostructural (machine and cardio), and oxidative (aerobic system), each a placement percentile from official 2026 Open and Quarterfinals results plus all prior Games. Because a 7.2km run also rewards a light frame, we scale that aerobic score by power-to-weight using each athlete's body mass. It is a fit read for a run, not a predicted finish. A great profile still has to be run on the dirt Wednesday.

title: What Dave Castro Has Already Told Us About the 2026 Games
dek: The hopper is back for a live Friday-night draw, swimming moves to a pool, and the Ranch is lurking. A sourced rundown of every reveal and tease.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: A sourced rundown of what Dave Castro has revealed and teased about the 2026 CrossFit Games programming: the returning hopper, a pool swim, cycling, the Rogue Pig and Snail, and the Ranch.

blocks.text: Dave Castro tells you about the Games for months before they start, in teasers, ranch videos and offhand comments. The trick is separating what is **confirmed** from what is a hint, because he plants misdirection on purpose. Here is what we actually know about the 2026 programming, with the source on every line.
The headline: the original hopper returns

Castro announced that the original Games hopper, the old peanut roaster used to pick the very first workout at the Ranch in 2007, is back. A workout gets **drawn live from it on the morning of Friday, July 24** and tested on the individuals under the lights at SAP Center that night. Athletes reacted fast: Taylor Self called it sick, and Jayson Hopper wrote, "let me pull from it, its only right."
Confirmed

items: **Swimming is back, in a pool.** Not open water. Presented by TYR, most likely at the Morgan Hill Outdoor Sport Center, the 2020 Games swim venue.
**Cycling returns** as part of the individual off-site opening, in the Games tradition of a Ride bike test. Distance and bike not yet announced.

**The competition is four days for individuals: Wednesday July 22 through Sunday July 26.** It opens at off-site Bay Area locations on the 22nd, livestreamed but not open to the public, before three arena days at SAP Center.
**The Rogue Pig and Snail return.** The Pig is a heavy rubber-encased block; the Snail is shaped like a hay bale but partly filled with sand that shifts as it rolls.
**20 scored events, the most in Games history**, on the Games 20th anniversary.

blocks.text: Teased (read with caution)

items: **Big Bob, on the street.** Walking SAP Center, Castro floated a team drag race "sprinting Big Bob down Barack Obama" Boulevard, calling it epic. A hint, not a confirmation.
**An outdoor run on closed roads.** He measured a turnaround about 200 yards down Barack Obama Boulevard with a trundle wheel, hinting at a roughly 400-yard looped street course.

**Extra days at the Ranch.** Castro said three SAP Center days does not mean a three-day Games: there "could be additional days that are not available for spectators to watch," read widely as non-spectator competition at the Aromas ranch.
**A possibly-new movement.** Asked if 2026 brings a new movement, he said he does not believe truly new movements exist, but on a previously-unprogrammed one answered "Possibly."
**A programming handoff.** On a CF Network show he said he is considering handing event programming to someone else this year, without naming who.

blocks.text: The throughline is the Ranch. Two Behind the Scenes videos show Castro testing 2026 events with athlete Rafael Sancen at Aromas in the weeks before the Games, so whatever lands in San Jose is being prototyped on the same dirt where the hopper was first drawn in 2007.

title: Who Actually Has the Engine to Win San Jose?
dek: The aerobic engines most likely to hold up across 20 events and 4 days.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: The 2026 CrossFit Games qualifiers with the strongest aerobic engine, ranked by oxidative, monostructural and sustained-output performance percentiles from official competition results.

blocks.text: San Jose is 20 scored events over 4 days, July 22-26 (SAP Center arena days July 24-26). That format does not reward one big lift or one fast sprint. It rewards the athlete whose output holds up on day four the same way it did on day one. So before we argue about who wins, ask a narrower question: who actually has the engine to survive it? The numbers below answer that, using only aerobic-system, monostructural, and sustained-output performance profiles.
The Men: Two Names Tied at the Top

Justin Medeiros and Roman Khrennikov share the highest oxidative score in the men's field at **79.3**. They get there differently. Khrennikov pairs that with the best monostructural mark of any man here at 80.7 and a sustained-output score of 78.5, the engine of a two-time Games runner-up who grinds rather than fades. Medeiros sits a hair behind on the machine work (77.8) but his profile is the most balanced of the group, with capacity at 78.9 and a Games title already on the record.

His engine score of 73.6 actually outruns his overall capacity of 70.2, which tells you the aerobic side is carrying him further than his average event finish suggests. Khrennikov is the inverse: the best engine among the men attached to a projected rank of 15, a reminder that a profile is not a placement. Patrick Vellner is the one to flag with caution. The aerobic read is strong at 74.6, but his sustained-output score sags to 65.5, the lowest of the six, the kind of split that gets found in a 20-event grind.
The Women: The Champion Type Versus the Top Seed

On the women's side the oxidative leader is Haley Adams at **76.0**, and she does not stop there. Her sustained-output score of 81.9 is the highest engine number in either division, paired with a 79.3 on the machines. A four-time Games athlete, she profiles as the kind of competitor a long format favors. What stands out is the gap: Adams projects 13th overall, yet no one in this group has a bigger engine. title: Prep Watch: 10 Days Out, What the Whole Field Is Drilling
dek: The 2026 field is deep in final prep and posting it. Here is what every revealed test demands, the ring skills everyone is grinding, and who our model reads as built for the hottest movement of the weekend.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: With the 2026 CrossFit Games about 10 days out (competition July 22-26, San Jose), athletes are deep in final prep and the training content is everywhere. Dave Castro has revealed enough - the CrossFit Total, a 7.2km Ranch trail run, a returning pool, and two never-tested ring skills - that the field's focus is clear. We break down what is hot, what each test demands, and who our model reads as built for it.

blocks.text: Ten days out from San Jose and the 2026 field is in the loud part of prep, all over your feed. The reason it is easy to read what they are drilling: **Dave Castro has already tipped most of the weekend.** We know Events 3, 4 and 5 are the CrossFit Total, Event 2 is a 7.2km Ranch trail run, a pool is back in play, and Sunday hides two ring skills the Games have never tested. Here is what is hot, what each test actually asks for, and who our model reads as built for it.
What's Hot: The Ring Skills

The single biggest talking point of the buildup is the pair of still-rings skills Castro unveiled on July 10: a **ring muscle-up straight into a forward roll to support**, and a **backward roll to support**. Here is the tell on how much the field cares: the reveal actually landed *after* athletes had already been spotted testing the movements on Instagram, and CrossFit followed with an official movement feature. Nobody is walking in cold. The whole field already owns the base - strict ring muscle-ups, skin-the-cats, strict ring handstand push-ups - and has had two weeks to drill the two additions, so this is not a wildcard nobody can do. It rewards the sharpest gymnasts and the cleanest technicians.
The Run Nobody Got to Train Indoors

Event 2, **Ranch 7200**, is a 7,200-meter trail run for time on the Aromas hills, about 4.5 miles of dirt and climbing. The catch that explains all the trail-miles content right now: the entire 2026 season was indoor, machine-and-barbell racing, so nobody has a measured trail time. On corrected competition vitals our model reads **Justin Medeiros** at the top on the best engine-to-mass blend, ahead of Ricky Garard and James Sprague. The biggest engine in the field, Roman Khrennikov, pays a real mass tax over 4.5 miles of climbing.
The Total: It's Max-Out Season

Events 3 to 5 are **The CrossFit Total**: a 1-rep-max back squat, strict shoulder press and deadlift, each scored as its own 50-point event. That is why the prep footage is full of heavy singles. The women's deadlift board just got a real-competition refresh - **Aimee Cringle** pulled 197 kg (435 lb) at the World Fitness Project - while the men's Total leans on **Nick Mathew**'s size. The strict press is the wild card: almost nobody in the field has real strict-press data, so it is the single lift most likely to scramble the order.
And a Pool Is Back

CrossFit confirmed swimming returns in a controlled pool for 2026, which pulls the proven water athletes back into the conversation after years of the swim being an open-water lottery. In a pool, technique and turns reward the handful of genuine swimmers in the field rather than the biggest engine.
Who to Watch on the Hot Skill

items: **Patrick Vellner and Victor Hoffer (men)** - the field's two former competitive artistic gymnasts. The new rolls are the closest thing to home court for anyone here; Hoffer trained federation-level gymnastics from age 3.
**Madeline Sturt and Abigail Domit (women)** - a rings specialist with teaching-level control and a USAG Level 9 artistic gymnast. Rotation and support are second nature.
**Colten Mertens** - plays in the United Grid League, where the backward roll to support is a standard skill. One of the two "new" movements may not be new to him at all.
**Roman Khrennikov** - an Olympic-reserve gymnastics base makes the rings a strength; his one tax this weekend is the run, not the rolls.

title: Event 13: The 500m Sprint - Whose Speed Wins?
dek: The Games just published a 500-meter sprint as Individual Event 13. The Games have run this test before - a 550-yard sprint in 2021 - and the real results reshuffle the model: the field already has a sprint champion in it.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: Individual Event 13 of the 2026 CrossFit Games is a 500-meter sprint, published on the official workouts page July 16. The Games ran a near-identical test in 2021 (the 550-yard sprint) and a track meet in 2024, and the verified results move the board: Guilherme Malheiros won the 2021 sprint outright, Ricky Garard won 2024 Track and Field, Khrennikov took 3rd there, and Haley Adams owns the best women's sprint resume in the field. History first, model second.

blocks.text: The reveals keep coming. The official Games workouts page just published **Individual Event 13: a 500-meter sprint**, full stop. No barbell, no rig, no strategy layer to hide behind: one maximal run. It is the first pure footrace-at-speed this field has faced at the Games, and it lands in the back half of the weekend, when 12 events of fatigue have already been banked.
What 500 Meters Actually Tests

Five hundred meters sits in the nastiest spot on the energy-system map. It is too long to be a pure phosphagen burst and far too short to settle into an aerobic rhythm: for athletes this size, it is roughly **75 to 100 seconds of maximal output**, which is peak **glycolytic** territory, the pathway that produces the burn and the bear that jumps on your back at the 300-meter mark. Pacing it is a razor: go out too hot and the last 150 meters becomes survival; too conservative and the heat is gone. Expect the field to cover the first 200 fast and then race who slows down least.
The Model Read: Men

Here is what the model alone misses: **the Games have already run this race.** Individual Event 3 of the 2021 Games was a **550-yard sprint** - 503 meters, virtually this exact test - and **Guilherme Malheiros won it outright** in 1:15.37, edging the field in a photo finish. **Patrick Vellner took 3rd** in that same race and **Saxon Panchik 4th**. Then in 2024, the **Track and Field** event (a 1,600m run plus a sprint-and-sandbag course at Farrington Field) went to **Ricky Garard**, who won both parts outright with a 1:04.89 sprint course; **Roman Khrennikov ran 3rd** there, so do not let his 103 kg fool you - the man moves. The honest note cuts the other way too: **Justin Medeiros**, who tops the pure model blend, finished 11th in the 2021 sprint and 25th in 2024 Track and Field. On real footraces, the résumés speak.

title: Event 15: The Speed Snatch Triple, and the 305-lb Elephant
dek: The Games just republished the 2020 Snatch Speed Triple, same name, same bars, 285 up top. One man in this field has snatched 305 in Games competition, and he also just topped our sprint board. Guilherme Malheiros, this is your event.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: Individual Event 15 of the 2026 CrossFit Games is the Speed Snatch Triple: three sets of 3 ascending snatches under 1, 2 and 3-minute caps, finishing at 285 lb men / 185 lb women. It is a rerun of the 2020 Games event of the same name, which echoed the 2015 Snatch Speed Ladder. We ground the read in verified Games history: Malheiros won the 2021 1RM Snatch at 305, Adler took 2nd in the 2020 running, Vellner has 290 in competition, and on the women side Hannah Black owns the most recent big verified snatch in the field.

blocks.text: The 20th-anniversary programming keeps reaching into the archive. The official workouts page just published **Individual Event 15, the Speed Snatch Triple**: 3 snatches with a 1-minute cap, 3 more with a 2-minute cap, 3 more with a 3-minute cap, every bar heavier than the last, finishing at **285 lb for the men and 185 lb for the women**. If that sounds familiar, it should: **this is the 2020 Games event, same name, same loads**, the elimination ladder where Mat Fraser missed his first attempt at the final 285 bar, recovered on the spot, and still won. That event itself echoed the 2015 Snatch Speed Ladder. The Games have run this test twice; we know exactly what it rewards.
What the Ladder Actually Tests

This is not a 1-rep-max event and it is not a metcon: it is **maximal weightlifting done fast, under a clock, repeatedly**. Nine snatches, every one heavier, with caps tight enough that there is no time to reset, breathe, and treat each bar like a platform lift. The athletes who survive it are the ones whose openers are so far inside their max that 265 moves like an empty bar, and whose technique holds when the heart rate is high. It rewards a verified heavy snatch, and it punishes anyone whose paper max was set fresh on a good day.
The Men: The 305-lb Elephant in the Room

Start with the verified history. **Guilherme Malheiros won the 2021 Games 1-rep-max snatch at 305 lb**, twenty pounds over this event's final bar, and he just topped our Event 13 sprint read because he **won the 2021 550-yard sprint** too. Speed plus snatch is not a coincidence for him; it is his signature, and this event is both at once. **Jeffrey Adler took 2nd in this exact event in 2020**. **Patrick Vellner** put 290 overhead in that same 2021 snatch event, also above the final bar, and **Saxon Panchik** (285 in 2021) and **Justin Medeiros** (285, plus 5th in the 2020 running) are right at it. The honest asterisk: **Dallin Pepper (308), Jayson Hopper (305) and Austin Hatfield (305)** all self-report maxes over the final bar, but those are profile numbers, not platform results - this ladder is where paper maxes get audited.

title: Event 7: Swim Standard - Whose Swim Holds Up?
dek: The Day 1 closer is 500 meters of pool swimming broken by 100 burpees, for time. Swimming decided Games leaderboards for a decade before it vanished. Now it is back, and history says it shreds the board.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: Individual Event 7 is Swim Standard: for time, 15-minute cap, a descending swim-and-burpee ladder (200m swim / 40 burpees / 150 / 30 / 100 / 20 / 50 / 10) in a 25-meter pool. It is the first Games swim event since 2022. Our own almanac shows swimming was a Games staple from 2011 to 2019, and the two closest precedents are the 2013 Pool (first 25-yard pool swim) and the 2014 Beach (swim plus burpees, won by Olympic sailing gold medalist Anna Tunnicliffe). Swim events reward a background you either have or you do not, and they produce some of the widest time gaps in the sport.

blocks.text: The official workouts page confirmed the Day 1 closer, and it is the one nobody in this field could fake: **Swim Standard**. For time, under a 15-minute cap: a 200-meter swim, 40 burpees, a 150-meter swim, 30 burpees, a 100-meter swim, 20 burpees, a 50-meter swim, 10 burpees. That is 500 meters of pool swimming, in 25-meter lengths, cut into a descending ladder by 100 total burpees. It streams exclusively on FloElite, and it is the first Games swim event since the 2022 Rinse N Repeat pool intervals.
Why the Swim Is the Great Equalizer

Swimming is the one skill in the sport that does not transfer from land. You can build a huge engine on the rower, the bike and the run and still be genuinely slow in the water, because swim speed lives in technique and comfort, not just fitness. The burpees make it meaner: you climb out of the pool, drop to the deck for a breathless set, then push back off the wall with your heart rate pinned and no ability to control your breathing underwater. Panic is a real factor. The athletes with a swim background will look calm and long in the water while the rest thrash.
The Pool Detail That Matters: 25-Meter Lengths

Five hundred meters in a 25-meter pool is 20 lengths and 19 turns. Every wall is a chance to gain or lose a body length depending on whether you can push off tight and streamlined or come in clumsy and stand up. The ladder is built smart, too: the longest swim (200m) comes first when you are freshest, and both the swims and the burpee sets shrink as the fatigue climbs, so the back half is a test of who can still move when the shoulders are shot.
History First: The Water Has Always Shredded the Board

This is not new territory for the Games, and our almanac makes the pattern obvious. Swimming was a fixture from 2011 through 2019, when the Games opened in the water almost every single year. Two precedents matter most here. The 2013 Pool, at the Woollett Aquatics Center, was the first true pool swim in Games history and it used 25-yard segments, the direct ancestor of this 25-meter pool test. And the 2014 Beach paired swimming with burpees and kettlebell thrusters, the same swim-plus-burpee shape you are watching now.

The winners tell you everything about how these events reward. The 2014 swim event was won on the women side by Anna Tunnicliffe, an Olympic gold medalist, in sailing. A water athlete to her core. Across the whole 2011 to 2019 run, swim mornings routinely produced surprise event winners and buried strength specialists who had no answer once the venue changed from the barbell to the buoy.
What It Means for the Standings

Day 1 has already run the 2007 Hopper, a 7,200-meter trail run, the full CrossFit Total and a bicycle race. Legs and grip are cooked, and the swim rewards a completely different system, which is exactly why it can flip the board. The strength men who owned the Total have no edge in the water. An unheralded swimmer can bank the day of their life. Expect one of the widest time spreads of the weekend: swim events regularly separate the field by a minute or more from top to bottom.
We will post the official podium and the updated overall the moment it scores. History says the name at the top may surprise you.

title: Women's Day 1: Cringle's Takeover, Campbell's Swim, and a Board That Would Not Sit Still
dek: Seven events in one day, and the women's leaderboard changed hands three times before Aimee Cringle ran away with it. How the board actually moved, who did the moving, and who to watch when Day 2 opens.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: The women completed all seven Day 1 events. Aimee Cringle ends on top with 458 points and a 38-point cushion after winning three events (the Ranch run, the deadlift and the bike), but she started the day 10th. The lead changed hands from Sturt to Adams to Cringle across the opening events. Lucy Campbell was a metronome at second before demolishing the swim by 69 seconds. Full event-by-event shake-up, the standouts, and the Day 2 watch list - every number verified against the official leaderboard.

blocks.text: Seven scored events in a single day is the most brutal opening the CrossFit Games have ever programmed, and the women's leaderboard treated it like a slalom. The overall lead changed hands three times across the first four events - Sturt, then Adams, then Sturt again, then Cringle - a Swiss rookie cracked the top three in the opening events, and the athlete who ends the day in front - **Aimee Cringle, 458 points** - was sitting **10th** after the very first event. Here is how the board actually moved.
The Takeover: Aimee Cringle

Cringle did not win the opener. She did not even come close: the 2007 Hopper (a 1,000m row into pull-ups and push jerks) left her 10th, and on a normal day that is a hole you spend the weekend digging out of. Instead she won the next thing that mattered and never looked back. She took the **7,200m Ranch run** outright, then the **deadlift** (425 lb), then the **bike race** - three event wins in three completely different domains. Endurance, max strength, and a leg-burning time trial, all won by the same 27-year-old from the Isle of Man who finished 8th here a year ago. She took the overall lead after the shoulder press and pushed it to a 38-point gap by nightfall. That is not a hot streak. That is range.
The Shake-Up, Event by Event
This is the part that makes a Day 1 fun, so let us walk the board the way it actually happened.

**After Event 1 (Hopper):** Madeline Sturt on top, winning the opener in 8:03. Lucy Campbell 2nd, Swiss rookie Aline Wirz a stunning 3rd. Cringle 10th, Alex Gazan 12th - the strength athletes buried, the engines up front.

**After Event 2 (Ranch 7200):** the run flipped it. Cringle won it in 40:42 with Haley Adams right behind (41:15), and Adams' Hopper-plus-run combination briefly put the **veteran into the overall lead**. Cringle surged to 5th. This was still anyone's day.

**Through the CrossFit Total (Events 3-5):** the strength block scrambled everything, twice. Quarterfinals winner **Kyra Milligan stole the back squat at 370 lb**, which nudged Sturt back into the overall lead. Then the shoulder press turned it over again: **Gazan won it at 170**, Sturt could only manage 27th, and Cringle inherited the lead she would not surrender. She slammed the door by winning the **deadlift at 425** to close the Total. When the barbell was loaded away, Cringle was 1st overall and the specialists had made their mark and slid back down.

**After Event 6 (Bike):** Cringle again, 19:10, her third win - and one of the closest finishes of the day behind her, with Emma Lawson (19:17.29) edging Campbell (19:17.30) for second by one hundredth of a second.
**After Event 7 (Swim):** Campbell's turn, and it was not close. More on that below.
Who Did Well

**Lucy Campbell (2nd, 420)** was the most consistent athlete on the floor. Read her overall rank through the day: 2nd, 2nd, 2nd, 2nd, then 4th, 3rd, 2nd. A metronome. The 2025 Games runner-up and reigning Open champion never had the single best event until the water, and then she had the best event by a mile. She is 38 points back and has the most complete resume in the chase.

**Madeline Sturt (3rd, 407)** won the opener and led early; the Australian engine and gymnastics are real. She faded only where you would expect, giving back ground in the swim (9th), but a podium spot after Day 1 continues a career-best arc for an athlete who was out of the Games entirely from 2020 to 2023.

**Haley Adams (4th, 372)** wore the overall lead for a moment after the run and stayed glued to the top five all day. The 2018 Fittest Teen keeps compounding a comeback most people did not expect after her 2023 step-away.

**Emma Lawson (5th, 364)** did the quiet thing that wins weekends: she climbed. Seventh, seventh, seventh, then a steady grind up to fifth by the swim. The youngest woman ever to podium at the Games (2nd in 2023 at age 18) sat out all of 2025 with a back injury. She looks healthy, and healthy Lawson is a problem for everyone above her.

**Alex Gazan (6th, 325)** is the wildcard. She won the shoulder press, took second on the deadlift, and owns one of the heaviest barbells in the field - then the bike (25th) reminded everyone why the Total is only three of twenty events. If Day 2 goes heavy, she is dangerous.
The Swim Was the Great Equalizer, Exactly As Promised

**We said before Event 7** that swimming is the one skill that does not transfer from land fitness, and that it reliably shreds a CrossFit leaderboard. It did. **Campbell won the Swim Standard in 10:55 - 69 seconds clear of the field** (Paige Rodgers 12:04, Danielle Brandon 12:18). That is not a CrossFitter who swims. That is a **former international swimmer** doing her actual sport, and the gap showed it. It cut the other way for the non-swimmers: Adams took 8th in the water, Sturt 9th, Wirz 14th, each bleeding points they had banked on the barbell and the run. Preparation meets the pool, and the pool does not care about your back squat.
People to Watch on Day 2

**Cringle** leads, but a 38-point cushion after 7 of 20 events is a headline, not a trophy. Her range is the real reason to believe: an athlete who can win a 7km run and a max deadlift on the same day does not have an obvious hole to attack.

**Campbell** is the hunter. Nearly the same points profile as the leader, and the deepest big-stage resume in the group. If the arena days bring classic barbell-and-gymnastics couplets, expect her to close.

**The 4-through-8 cluster is tight** - Adams (372) down to Arielle Loewen (300) is separated by a single strong event. Loewen, a 2023 podium finisher, already clawed from 16th back to 8th on the strength of a 4th-place swim. That group will reorder fast.

**And keep an eye on the rookie.** Aline Wirz, 32, sits 7th after being diagnosed with a C6 neck fracture roughly five weeks before her semifinal. Seventh at the CrossFit Games after Day 1, on that backstory, is one of the quiet stories of the weekend.
Seven events down, thirteen to go. The board churned this much in one day - so hold your final takes. The men's Day 1 recap is next, and their swim has not even scored yet.

title: Men's Day 1: Jay Crouch Led Wire to Wire, Then the Water Took It
dek: The same story as the women, told louder. Jay Crouch led after every one of the first six events, the swim knocked him to fourth, and James Sprague inherited the lead. How the men's board moved, and who is still alive with thirteen events to go.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: The men finished all seven Day 1 events. Jay Crouch led the overall after every event from the Hopper through the bike, then a 19th-place swim dropped him to 4th on the final event of the day. James Sprague (the 2024 champion) took over the lead at 418 (officials later revised some Day 1 scores), ahead of Dallin Pepper (413), with two-time champion Justin Medeiros 3rd. Ty Jenkins won the swim, Colten Mertens swept the Total's squat and press, and the reigning champion Jayson Hopper sits 8th. Top five separated by 28 points. Every number verified against the official leaderboard.

blocks.text: If you want the shape of the men's Day 1 in one sentence: Jay Crouch led after every single event from the opener through the bike, and then he went swimming. The Australian sat first overall for six straight events - a wire-to-wire day in the making - until the Swim Standard caught him, dropped him to 19th on the event, and knocked him to **4th overall** on the last test of the night. Behind him, **James Sprague inherited the lead.** Here is how the board moved.
Wire to Wire, Then the Water

Crouch was magnificent for most of the day. He won the 2007 Hopper outright in 7:11, took 3rd on the Ranch run, and did the quietly harder thing through the strength block - he never won a lift, but he never bled enough points to lose the lead either. Six events, six times atop the overall board. Then the pool did what the pool does. A 19th-place swim is a small crack on most days; on the final event of a seven-event marathon, with the field this tight, it cost him three spots and the lead. He is 4th, 27 points off the top, and he still had one of the best days on the floor. That is how brutal this opening was.
The Shake-Up, Event by Event
**After Event 1 (Hopper):** Crouch on top, winning the opener in 7:11. Colten Mertens 2nd, Saxon Panchik 3rd. Dallin Pepper, who ends the day 2nd overall, opened in 17th.
**After Event 2 (Ranch 7200):** Ricky Garard won the 7,200m run in 39:33, with Sprague 2nd (39:43) and Crouch 3rd (39:52) - three men inside 20 seconds after 4.5 miles. Crouch held the overall lead.

**Through the CrossFit Total (Events 3-5):** the strength kings had their moment. **Mertens swept the first two lifts** - a 555 lb back squat and a 260 lb shoulder press - and **Patrick Vellner won the deadlift at 605 lb** at age 36. Crouch, no one's idea of a strength specialist, simply refused to fall apart (14th squat, 11th press, 18th deadlift) and carried his lead straight through the barbell.

**After Event 6 (Bike):** a photo finish - Moritz Fiebig won the Grass Oval by 0.14 of a second over Pepper, with the top five inside three-quarters of a second. Crouch was 3rd and, yes, still led overall.
**After Event 7 (Swim):** the day flipped. More below.
Who Did Well

**James Sprague (1st, 414)** did what champions do: he was never worse than good and he was there at the end. The 2024 Fittest Man on Earth ground out a 2nd on the run, a 2nd on the deadlift and a top-six swim, and when Crouch cracked, Sprague was the one standing in front. He leads Day 1 by five points after the officials' revised scoring (418 to Pepper's 413).

**Dallin Pepper (2nd, 413)** authored the best climb of the day. Seventeenth after the Hopper, then 9th, 10th, 8th, 6th, 4th, and finally 2nd - a relentless march up the board capped by a 3rd-place swim. The 2024 runner-up and three-time teen world champion is one point off the lead and trending the right way.

**Justin Medeiros (3rd, 392)** reminded everyone the two-time champion does not have obvious holes. He sat mid-pack early, took 2nd in the swim, and slid into the final podium spot. Quiet, efficient, dangerous.

**Ricky Garard (5th, 386)** won the run and never left the top five. The 2025 runner-up, four years removed from a doping ban he came back to erase, keeps stacking consistent finishes - exactly the profile that wins long weekends.

**And the strength men made their statement:** Mertens took two event wins in the Total and Vellner took a third; both will be salivating if Day 2 brings heavy barbell. Mertens sits 9th only because the bike (0 points) and the swim buried an otherwise huge day.
The Swim Was the Great Equalizer, Again

Same lesson the women taught a few hours earlier. **Ty Jenkins - a former three-time teen world champion and one of the youngest men in the field - won the Swim Standard outright in 11:09**, ahead of Medeiros (11:23) and Pepper (11:49). And it cut the legs out from under the leader: Crouch's 19th in the water is the single reason Sprague is wearing the overall lead tonight instead of him. The pool does not care who led on the barbell.
People to Watch on Day 2

**The whole top five is live.** Sprague (418), Pepper (413), Medeiros (388), Crouch (387) and Garard (386) are packed into 32 points. One event reorders all of them. This is not a race with a runaway - it is a knife fight.

**Where is the champ?** Reigning Fittest Man on Earth Jayson Hopper sits 8th (304). He had no bye and had to requalify the hard way after a groin injury, and Day 1 was clearly a grind for him. But defending champions do not usually stay 8th - watch whether he climbs when the arena events start.

**And watch Crouch's response.** Leading wire to wire and losing it on the last event of the day can break an athlete or light a fire. He has the engine and the gymnastics for the arena. How he answers Day 2 will tell us whether Day 1 was a fluke of one bad discipline or a real ceiling.

Seven down, thirteen to go, three former champions in the top eight and none of them running away. Hold your final takes - the men's board proved today it can turn over on a single event. The end-of-day data breakdown is next.

title: The Rookie Report: How the 15 First-Timers Handled Day 1
dek: Six men, nine women, zero Games experience between them, and a seven-event opener that would rattle a veteran. Three of them still walked off an event podium. Here is how every 2026 rookie handled Day 1.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: The 2026 field has 15 Games rookies (6 men, 9 women). On a brutal seven-event opening day, three of them reached an event podium: Aline Wirz (3rd, Hopper), Ella Wilkinson (3rd, Ranch 7200) and Dylan Hamming (3rd, shoulder press). Wirz sits 7th overall, the only rookie in the top 10, on the back of an elite engine and despite a rough CrossFit Total. The class also skews young (Miley Wade is 18, the youngest in the field) and it was not spared by the day - Hannah Black fought ankle trouble on the run. Every number verified against the official leaderboard.

blocks.text: Fifteen athletes walked into the 2026 CrossFit Games with zero individual Games experience - six men, nine women - and the sport did not ease them in. Seven scored events in a single day is the most brutal opener ever programmed, the kind of day that rattles athletes who have done this for a decade. And yet three of these first-timers walked off an event podium. Here is how the whole rookie class handled Day 1.
Three Rookies, Three Podiums

Start with the headline. **Aline Wirz took 3rd in the opening Hopper** (8:16), behind only Madeline Sturt and Lucy Campbell. **Ella Wilkinson ran to 3rd in the Ranch 7200** (42:16), a 7,200-meter trail race, beaten only by Aimee Cringle and Haley Adams. And on the men side, **Dylan Hamming pressed 245 lb for 3rd in the shoulder press**, one rung below Colten Mertens and Ricky Garard. Three rookies who did not merely survive an event - they beat almost every veteran in it.
The Rookie of Day 1: Aline Wirz

Switzerland's Wirz, 32, sits **7th overall** after Day 1, the only rookie in either division inside the top 10. Her card tells you exactly who she is: 3rd on the Hopper, 4th on the bike, an engine that belongs at this level. The CrossFit Total exposed the gap - 27th, 29th and 29th on the three lifts - but she had banked so much on the mono-structural events that she held a top-seven spot through the barbell block anyway. And remember the backstory: she was diagnosed with a C6 neck fracture roughly five weeks before her semifinal. Seventh at the CrossFit Games after Day 1, on that timeline, is the story of this rookie class.
The Young Guns

Three of these rookies are barely out of the teen ranks. **Miley Wade, at 18 the youngest athlete in the entire field**, took 8th on the Ranch run and sits 25th - completely at home. **Iceland's Bergros Bjornsdottir, 19**, was the steadiest rookie on the floor: a best of 8th on the back squat and nothing worse than 24th across all seven events, good for 15th overall on debut. And **Chile's Benjamin Reyes, 21**, had the hardest day of the group, but he made it here, and he is 21. This class has a future.
The Men's Class

Georgia's **Nika Maisuradze** led the rookie men in 17th, with a pair of 6th-place finishes - the Ranch run and the deadlift - that point to a real all-around base. Spain's **Luis Cuellar**, 19th, saved his best for last with a 5th in the Swim Standard, a rookie who can actually swim in a field where most cannot. And **Dylan Hamming**, at 33 the oldest rookie in the field, announced himself on the barbell with that 3rd-place press. Different ages, different tools, same result: they belonged.
Day 1 Also Took a Toll

The opener was punishing, and not everyone came through it clean. Per BoxRox's Day 1 coverage, Henrik Haapalainen raced the 7,200m Ranch carrying an Achilles injury and Anika Greer competed on an injured ankle. Among the rookies, **Hannah Black dealt with ankle trouble on the same trail run** and did not post a scored result on the bike. The steep Ranch climbs forced multiple athletes to walk sections of the course. Day 1 was a test of durability as much as fitness, and the newcomers felt every bit of it.
What Day 2 Holds

The arena events (8 through 12) reward a different toolkit than Day 1's strength-and-engine poles: high-skill gymnastics, barbell cycling, mixed triplets under fatigue. That is neutral-to-good news for the rookies who lost ground on the Total, like Wirz and Wilkinson, and a real test for the ones who leaned on it. First-timers carry no scar tissue from a bad Games day and none of the pressure of defending a ranking. Watch whether Wirz can hold the top 10 when the barbell gets technical - and whether one of these names sneaks another event podium indoors.
Fifteen first-timers walked into the deepest field the sport has ever assembled, and three of them left Day 1 standing on an event podium. Whatever Friday brings, this class arrived.
